<div class="wrap" markdown="1">

{% raw %}
The roster is the league's list of players. Attendance, reports, claims and every rotation work from it, so a name must be on the roster before anyone can be confirmed for an event or claim it. Managing it needs the **Manage the roster** permission; approving claims needs **Review claims** (officers have both by default).

## The roster manager

Run `/roster` in an officers' channel. It posts a roster panel that stays there for officers to use, 15 players a page, with **⏮ First**, **◀ Prev**, **Next ▶** and **Last ⏭**. **Inactive** and **On leave** show or hide those players.

Pick a player from the menu to open the **player editor**, privately: only you see it, and the shared panel stays as it is for everyone else.

## Adding a player

Press **Add** and type the in-game name exactly as the game shows it (and, with DC Dark Legion, their power if you know it). A name already on the roster is refused, whatever its capitals.

## The player editor

**Core**: the name, whether they are active, on leave, their previous leagues and who referred them. In a server with DC Dark Legion it also has power and rank, plus the **Train seats** and **Events** tabs for train seats and the events they can make. With two or more games that have player details, a menu on the Core tab picks which game's details to show.

- **Active** and **On leave** save the moment you press them.
- Everything else collects until you press **Review changes**, which shows before and after; **Confirm save** saves it.

**Renaming** a player carries their whole history with them: past attendance and awards follow the new name.

**Inactive** is for players who have left: they drop out of attendance lists, rotations and reports but keep their history. Prefer it to deleting.

**On leave** is temporary: rotations and team lists leave the player out until it is cleared. Players can set it themselves in `/my-profile`.

## The Claim tab: who a player is on Discord

A claim links a player to a Discord account. The Claim tab shows the link and lets you **Set link** or **Clear link** directly; these happen at once. Use it to move a character from one account to another, or to link someone who cannot use `/claim`.

## Approving claims

Members ask with `/claim`. Each request appears in your **Claim Requests** channel (or the Officer Log if that is not set) with three buttons:

- **✅ Approve**
- **✖️ Deny**
- **📝 Deny with reason**: the member sees your reason in a direct message.

The member is told the outcome by direct message (if their DMs are closed, the bot tells you so you can let them know). Only one officer can decide a request; anyone pressing afterwards is told it was already decided. A character that already belongs to someone else cannot be approved for another member: move it from the Claim tab instead.

`/claim-requests` lists the requests still waiting, if the notices have scrolled away -- claims and character requests both.

## Members' own characters

Each game's settings tab in `/guild-settings show` has **👤 Who adds characters**:

- **Members add their own**: members add their main and alts themselves (the usual way in games like World of Warcraft). A member not on the roster yet is added when they add their first character.
- **Members ask, an officer approves**: each new character waits. Its notice appears with the claim requests, with **Approve** and **Deny**; the member is told what you decided.
- **Officers only**: as before. DC Dark Legion starts here.

Whichever you choose, officers can always add, change or remove anyone's characters: open the player in `/roster`, go to the **Claim** tab and press **👤 Characters**. A player can have up to 10 characters in a game, and a character name is unique in a game on your server.

## Updating many players at once

**Bulk power** (DC Dark Legion) walks through the roster strongest first, a batch at a time: **Edit batch** opens a form with each player's current power filled in; change what has changed and leave the rest. **Finish** when done.

**📄 CSV** (premium plans) exports and imports the roster as a spreadsheet file:

- **📤 Export roster** gives you the current roster as a file. It is also the template for an import.
- **📥 Import a file** reads one back and shows a **preview** before anything changes: what will be updated, names it does not know (you choose which to add), and rows it could not read, with the reason.

Only the columns in your file change, and an empty cell changes nothing, so a file with just `name` and `power` updates power and nothing else. Players missing from the file are left alone. If someone edits the roster between your preview and your confirm, the import is refused rather than overwrite their change.

## From a member's name

Right-click a member, then **Apps → Edit player**, to open the player editor for the character they have claimed. With several claimed characters, it asks which.
